findings.current: The office of the Qinghai City Lord, now a headless corpse, was as impossibly spacious and luxurious as ever.
findings.defect: The officeholder is called the Qinghai Governor immediately afterward.
findings.rationale: Uses one title for the same deceased officeholder within the scene.
findings.replacement: The office of the Qinghai Governor, now a headless corpse, was as impossibly spacious and luxurious as ever.

findings.current:
Only one young, nameless disciple had made it back to Xining.

And even he had died along the way.
findings.defect: The disciple died after meeting scouts a hundred li west of Xining, not after reaching the city.
findings.rationale: Preserves his journey and death without contradicting the opening scene.
findings.replacement:
Only one young, nameless disciple had made it back toward Xining.

And even he had died along the way.
findings.source: Chapter 1090, account of the Beggars’ Sect disciples

findings.current: The qi of the Zaha Divine Technique enveloped his entire body.
findings.defect: After the introduction of two additional speakers, “his” has an unclear antecedent.
findings.rationale: Identifies whose qi is being described without changing the action.
findings.replacement: The qi of the Zaha Divine Technique enveloped Cheongpung’s entire body.
findings.source: Chapter 1094, arrival of the allied fighters

findings.defect: The supposed correction repeats the same identification.
findings.rationale: Removes a contradictory self-correction while retaining Taekyung’s recognition.

summary: Four actionable continuity and clarity issues: an inconsistent title, a mistaken arrival, an ambiguous pronoun, and a duplicated identification.
